newsitem.title: UK: Eurotunnel unveils bank debt deal.
newsitem.headline: Eurotunnel unveils bank debt deal.

text.p: Anglo-French channel tunnel operator Eurotunnel SA/Plc on Monday announced details of a crucial debt restructuring plan to save the troubled company from insolvency.

Under the terms of the deal Eurotunnel said it would restructure 8.7 billion pounds ($13.62 billion) of debt and unpaid interest owed to a syndicate of 225 banks. It also involves a debt-for-equity swap, under which existing shareholders will retain around 54.5 percent of the enlarged equity.
The restructuring plan, detailed in a statement, includes a debt-for-equity swap at 130 pence per share to reduce outstanding debt by one billion pounds.

Eurotunnel said a further 3.7 billion pounds of debt will be converted into new instruments created as part of the restructuring deal. It said existing shareholders would be able to participate in this issue but terms were not yet agreed.
The company said interest rates on the debt and new instruments are fixed for seven years at "significantly" below market rates.
Eurotunnel shares are due to resume trading on October 8. ($1=.6388 Pound)
